name: task-family

families.name: Code generation
families.definition: Create software code, tests, machine-readable configuration, database queries, or other artifacts intended for execution or parsing; exclude natural-language prompts for creative media.

families.name: Debugging and review
families.definition: Diagnose a technical failure, inspect existing code, review implementation quality, or recommend a fix to an existing technical artifact.

families.name: Writing
families.definition: Create original text whose main deliverable is communicative, literary, commercial, or professional prose; exclude prompts or specifications whose target output is visual, audio, video, or interactive media.

families.name: Editing and rewriting
families.definition: Transform, polish, shorten, translate, or otherwise revise text supplied by the user while preserving its core subject or intent.

families.name: Information and research
families.definition: Retrieve, explain, compare, evaluate, or synthesize facts, sources, or bodies of evidence into an informational answer.

families.name: How-to and advice
families.definition: Give practical instructions, recommendations, or guidance for accomplishing a concrete goal; the requested deliverable is advice, not a project plan.

families.name: Tutoring
families.definition: Teach through explicit learning-oriented scaffolding, practice, quizzing, feedback, or adaptation to a learner; a one-off request to explain a fact belongs to information and research.

families.name: Data and math
families.definition: Produce a calculation, proof, statistical analysis, structured-data transformation, or quantitative result; use tutoring only when learning interaction is the dominant request.

families.name: Planning and ideation
families.definition: Generate options, structure a project, develop a strategy, or sequence future work into a plan rather than merely explain how to perform one task.

families.name: Agentic tool use
families.definition: Actually inspect or change external state through tools, or coordinate a multi-step workflow that requires such actions; discussion or advice about tools alone belongs to the underlying task family.

families.name: Creative and media generation
families.definition: Create or direct visual, audio, video, interactive role-play, or other media, including natural-language prompts for a generative-media model; text-only prose intended for a reader remains writing.

families.name: Conversational, other, and outlier
families.definition: Social conversation, self-expression, unsupported or unsafe-to-classify requests, requests outside the listed families, or items without a dominant task family.

boundary_rules: Choose the family of the requested deliverable, not merely the topic, domain, or length of the answer.
When revising user-supplied text, choose editing-rewriting; when creating new prose from a topic or brief, choose writing.
Natural-language prompts for image, audio, video, or interactive-media generation are creative-media, not code-generation or writing.
A direct factual explanation is information-seeking; tutoring requires an explicit learning interaction such as scaffolding, practice, a quiz, feedback, or adaptation.
Research breadth and source count are recorded as an orthogonal evidence-scope dimension and do not create a separate family.
Agentic-tool-use requires actual or explicitly requested external-state action, not hypothetical instructions about using a tool.

migration.rationale: The original random-public ambiguous stratum contains a large code-generation versus writing cluster dominated by generative-media prompting, while research-synthesis is sparse and behaves as an unstable composite of informational breadth and output form.
